subject: Fix VST3 host-side spec violations: message passing, resizable GUIs, editor teardown
query_full:
Fix VST3 host-side spec violations: message passing, resizable GUIs, editor teardown

Serum2/Pigments crash Infinite as VST3 but not AU because three host-side
spec requirements were unmet:

- IHostApplication::createInstance was a stub returning kNoInterface
  unconditionally, so ComponentBase::allocateMessage() always returned null.
  This is the only channel for processor<->controller messaging beyond plain
  parameters (wavetable/spectrum displays, voice counts, sample loading);
  parameter-only effects never hit this path, which is why only big synths
  broke. Implements IMessage/IAttributeList by hand, matching the reference
  [file] semantics.

- IPlugFrame was never implemented and plugView->setFrame() was never
  called, so a plugin with a resizable GUI (Serum2) had no host object to
  ask for a resize.

- The editor's plugView->removed() was only ever called from
  PluginVST3Destroy, and even there it ran after the window had already
  closed. A closed-but-not-removed editor leaves the plugin's GUI timer
  armed against a view Infinite no longer considers open - the crash
  report that started this investigation is a CFRunLoopTimer callback with
  zero Infinite frames on the stack, exactly this shape. removed() now runs
  first, while the container view is still alive, on the attached()-failure
  path, on PluginVST3CloseEditor, and on PluginVST3Destroy; CloseEditor now
  fully detaches instead of merely hiding the window.

IPlugFrame::iid and IPlugView::iid are defined in the SDK's
[file], now added to the VST3 source list.

Connection-point proxying (item 4 of the same investigation, which changes
threading behavior) is a separate commit.

subject: Fix modulator cables being dropped by undo, redo and patch load
query_full:
Fix modulator cables being dropped by undo, redo and patch load

Modulator-into-modulator connections (Random -> Range to Range's `in`,
and every other node exposing a ModulatorInputSlot) are raw IModulator*
pointers rather than ImageCables, so restoring them goes through
ConnectGeometrySlot. That function only knew how to re-seat MathNode's
two pins, so every other modulator input cable was written into the
snapshot by BuildPatchData and then silently dropped on the way back in
- one undo anywhere on the canvas detached the cable, and the same hole
hit redo and opening a saved patch.

Replaces the MathNode special case with the generic
ModulatorInputSlot() accessor the live drag-to-connect path already
uses, and threads the source output index through: BuildPatchData knew
which output of a multi-output modulator was wired but discarded it, so
even MathNode's restored cables snapped back to output 0.

Affects 11 node types: Math, Compare, Range to Range, Smoothing,
Invert, Mod Depth, Mod Curve, CV to Pitch, Null Modulator, Envelope,
OSC Send.

INFINITE_UNDOTEST grows a registry-wide sweep rather than a
hand-written fixture, so a new modulator-input node cannot quietly
reintroduce the hole: 11 types swept, 0 lost with the fix, 11 lost
without it.

subject: Fix PortableFft::Inverse, port Molder off Accelerate, Windows icon and .infinite
query_full:
Fix PortableFft::Inverse, port Molder off Accelerate, Windows icon and .infinite

Four things, all needed before a Windows build can ship anything current.

PortableFft::Inverse was not the inverse of Forward (two defects):
  - RunCore built its twiddles at a negative angle and used them
    unconditionally, so Inverse ran the FORWARD kernel over a Hermitian-
    mirrored spectrum and returned the input TIME-REVERSED. Now takes an
    `inverse` flag that conjugates the twiddles.
  - Inverse passed mRe/mIm as RunCore's own input while RunCore writes them
    through a non-identity permutation, corrupting the data. Now stages into
    mStageRe/mStageIm, sized in Prepare() so the class stays allocation-free
    on the audio thread.
  - Scaling was also wrong in a way the class comment documented backwards.
    PaulStretchNode's normScale = 1/(N*1.5) is SHARED by both backends, so
    Inverse has to match vDSP_fft_zrip(FFT_INVERSE) exactly: unnormalised,
    yielding N*x. Dropped the stray 0.5 and the 1/N, and corrected the
    contract comment.

Verified against Accelerate at N = 32..16384: forward and inverse now both
match vDSP to 2.1e-07 worst relative error.

Added RunPortableFftFixture to RunDspTest (INFINITE_DSPTEST, exit-code gated,
runs headless in CI on BOTH platforms so macOS gates the Windows backend).
It asserts Forward's x2 zrip packing via a DC probe and the N*x round trip,
and names the time-reversal case explicitly. Confirmed it fails (exit 1) when
the twiddle bug is reintroduced - a regression test that cannot see the
regression is worthless.

[file] arrived from main with an unfenced <[file]> in
the SHARED source list, so it could not compile on Windows at all - and it
needs a working inverse transform, which is why the above had to come first.
All vDSP use was confined to FftContext; PortableFft's Forward/Inverse are
drop-ins for those exact ctoz/zrip/ztoc pairs, so the surrounding maths is
untouched and the Apple path is byte-identical.

Patches now save as .infinite on Windows. ".inf" is RESERVED there for Setup
Information files, so a saved patch showed up as "Setup Information", took the
OS setup icon, and double-clicking handed it to the installer machinery. That
association belongs to the system and must not be hijacked. Both extensions
are still accepted when opening, so patches stay portable both ways; only the
default for new saves differs. Also fixed the basename split to accept
backslashes.

Added src/platform/win/Infinite.rc: app icon (generated from the existing
assets/Infinite.iconset, all seven Explorer sizes down to 16px so list views
are not badly downscaled) plus a VERSIONINFO block, since an unsigned exe with
no version info looks maximally anonymous to SmartScreen.

macOS verified unchanged: DSPTEST OK exit 0, and AUDIOPARAMSWEEPTEST's failure
set is byte-identical to origin/main's (359 lines both, empty diff both ways).

subject: Fix Geometry Table grid pins: only the last-drawn cell was draggable
query_full:
Fix Geometry Table grid pins: only the last-drawn cell was draggable

ed::BeginPin()/EndPin() derive a pin's hit bounds from the enclosing
ImGui group's bounding box, anchored at the cursor position from before
BeginPin() and grown via the window's monotonic CursorMaxPos. The grid
jumps the cursor to each cell's absolute position via SetCursorScreenPos
without ever advancing the real layout cursor, so each successive pin's
group-derived bounds ballooned to include every prior cell - only the
last cell (bottom-right) ended up with bounds covering the whole grid,
so every drag started from it regardless of which cell was clicked.
Use ed::PinRect() to set each pin's bounds explicitly instead.

subject: Fix reverse video playback frame-rate collapse
query_full:
Fix reverse video playback frame-rate collapse

mPosition was never wrapped/clamped for negative speed, so it walked
past 0 forever — on macOS that meant tearing down and rebuilding the
AVAssetReader every frame while producing only frame 0; on Windows the
reader just stopped updating once position went negative.

Now mPosition wraps (loop) or clamps (no loop) on both sides. On
macOS, backward seeks target the requested time instead of always
restarting the reader at t=0, and the last few dozen decoded frames
are kept in a byte-capped cache so steady reverse playback pays for a
reader rebuild roughly once per cache window instead of once per
frame. Windows already seeks to the target rather than zero, so it's
left as-is.

subject: Fix instancing collapsing behind passthrough nodes, and dropped group matrix
query_full:
Fix instancing collapsing behind passthrough nodes, and dropped group matrix

InstanceOnPointsNode returns the single stamp mesh from GetMesh() and carries
its N placements separately, so consumers walk PassthroughSource() to find the
instancer and read GetInstanceGroupMatrix() to pick up a wrapping Transform's
rigid move. Two halves of that contract were being dropped:

- Null3D, Displacement and Wrap forwarded every other side-channel but not
  PassthroughSource(), so patching any of them after an Instance on Points
  drew one stamp instead of N instances, with no error anywhere. Null 3D is
  the clearest case - a node whose whole job is to be a no-op passthrough was
  destroying the instancing it passed through.
- Material, Set Color, Merge by Distance and Switcher 3D implemented
  PassthroughSource() without GetInstanceGroupMatrix(), so
  Instance on Points -> Transform -> Material -> Render 3D found the instancer
  but read an identity group matrix and drew the scatter back at the origin.

Both accessors now travel together on all seven nodes; Wrap forwards from
sourceInput (the stamp being wrapped), Switcher 3D from the same Active() slot
its PassthroughSource() returns so the two can't disagree.

Adds INSTANCESWEEPTEST, a fifth generic sweep in geometry-transform-sweep, so
this stays enforced as new geometry nodes are added rather than re-checked by
hand. Verified it fails on each of the two dropped overrides before the fix.
No revision plumbing needed: both consumers already compare the group matrix
directly ([file], [file]).
query_subject: Fix instancing collapsing behind passthrough nodes, and dropped group matrix

subject: Fix instanced selection overlay drawing at unit scale, and self-test stdout flush

Fix instanced selection overlay drawing at unit scale, and self-test stdout flush

Part 0 of [file]: the mini-viewport's orange
selection overlay drew the stamp's selected faces once at unit scale
(glDrawElements + uModel), floating over N real instances that ignored it,
because kSelectVertSrc had no aInstance input and mSelVao only bound attrib 0.

- kSelectVertSrc now takes aInstance/uInstanced and picks aInstance vs uModel

- LinkSelectionProgram binds attrib 2 ("aInstance") alongside the existing
  attrib 0.
- The selection draw block (not UpdateSelectionBuffer, which can run before
  mInstanceVbo is ever generated) now wires mSelVao's instance attribs to the
  already-populated mInstanceVbo when instanced, tracked by a new
  mSelInstanceAttribsOn flag mirroring mInstanceAttribsOn, and issues
  glDrawElementsInstanced instead of glDrawElements.
- Fixed the stale comment at the old [file]:94 claiming this
  mirrors a Render3DNode selection overlay - Render3DNode has none.

Also: fflush(stdout) before the shutdown path's std::_Exit(0). _Exit skips
the normal atexit stdio flush; only the INFINITE_EXITAFTER frame-count
branch had its own fflush. Every self-test that closes the window itself on

subject: Fix VST3/AU plugin note input being silently dropped
query_full:
Fix VST3/AU plugin note input being silently dropped

AudioNode's slot-aware SetNoteInbox(slot, inbox, cursor) default only
forwarded slot 0 to the single-slot overload. Nodes whose slot 0 is an
audio input put their note pin at slot 1 - AudioPluginNode,
WaveTerrainNode, ImageSpectralSynthNode - so the topology builder's call
was dropped on the floor: mNoteInbox stayed nullptr and the node was mute
no matter what note source was wired in. Forward every slot instead; the
builder only calls slots the node actually exposes, and Note Merge (the
one real multi-input consumer) overrides this anyway.

PLUGINSCANTEST and the audio param sweep both wired their inboxes by
calling the two-arg overload directly, bypassing the very dispatch that
was broken - which is how this shipped past them. Both now wire through
the slot-aware overload at the node's real slot; with the fix reverted,
PLUGINSCANTEST reports note-on peak=0.00000 FAIL.

subject: Fix app-wide hang from duplicate pin ids, and guard against it recurring
query_full:
Fix app-wide hang from duplicate pin ids, and guard against it recurring

The Wavetable node froze the app. Its two engine columns draw the same
control labels, and a discrete param's pin id comes from a hash of its
label alone (ImGui::PushID scopes widget ids, not these), so both engines
landed on one pin id. imgui-node-editor links a node's pins into a list as
they're emitted, so emitting one id twice in a frame made that list
circular - and every walk of it (the hit-test pass, the bounds pass, the
drag scan) is a plain `for (p = last; p; p = p->m_PreviousPin)`. The app
didn't crash, glitch or draw wrong: it spun at 100% CPU inside one frame,
forever, as soon as the cursor was over the canvas. Users saw only a
system "hang" report.

Three changes, at three depths:

- DiscreteSlotScope ([file]) gives a repeated sub-panel its own discrete
  namespace, so engine B's controls get their own slots. Engine 0 keeps the
  unscoped hash, so bindings in already-saved patches still resolve. This
  also fixes the user-visible half of the same collision: modulating engine
  A's filter was driving engine B's too.

- NodeBuilder::BeginPin refuses to relink an id already emitted this frame,
  turning any future collision into a warning instead of a freeze. Stamped
  with the ImGui frame index rather than m_IsLive, which Object's ctor sets
  true and so cannot distinguish a first emission from a repeat.

- PINDUPTEST spawns every registered node type with both param sections
  forced open and asserts zero duplicates. Verified against a negative
  control (it catches all 6 colliding Wavetable labels); 267 types clean
  with the fix. ROUNDTRIPTEST covers every type too but draws them
  collapsed, which is exactly why it never saw this.

Also: test runs (INFINITE_EXITAFTER) now create their window hidden and
unfocused. They were stealing focus mid-suite, and a slow frame in a
foreground window is what tripped WindowServer's 10-second watchdog into
writing the hang spindumps in the first place.
query_subject: Fix app-wide hang from duplicate pin ids, and guard against it recurring

subject: Fix a use-after-free on the Windows audio thread, and a per-restart handle leak
query_full:
Fix a use-after-free on the Windows audio thread, and a per-restart handle leak

Both were open items under [file] 1.9.

AudioInputCaptureRead runs on the audio render thread and was gated on
`running && sampleRate > 0.0`, but CaptureTapEngine::OnFormat wrote
sampleRate BEFORE ring.Init() - so between those two statements the render
thread could pass the gate and index ring.buffers while assign() was
reallocating it. The window reopened on every input-engine restart, which
PollAudioRecovery triggers on any device change. Readiness is now a single
atomic set only after the ring is allocated, and that is what the read path
gates on.

ThreadMain's bufferEvent was a local inside the SUCCEEDED(Initialize)
block and was never closed on any path out, leaking one event handle per

subject: Fix vertically mirrored Windows video export, and raise encode quality
query_full:
Fix vertically mirrored Windows video export, and raise encode quality

Two separate defects behind the same user report ("garbled, compressed,
upside down and flipped").

1. Every movie recorded on Windows came out vertically mirrored.
   Media Foundation's RGB32 input format defaults to bottom-up
   orientation - the GDI BITMAPINFOHEADER convention, signalled by a
   negative MF_MT_DEFAULT_STRIDE. ConfigureRecorderVideo never set that
   attribute, while RgbaBottomUpToBgraTopDown was already flipping GL's
   bottom-up readback into top-down rows, so the sink writer read a
   top-down buffer as bottom-up and mirrored the whole take. Set the
   attribute explicitly to a positive width * 4.

   [file] 1.7 covers stride on the decode side;
   the encode side was never checked. macOS is unaffected - AVFoundation
   takes a CVPixelBuffer with no orientation ambiguity.

2. The bitrate ladder was 0.08 bits per pixel per frame - roughly 5 Mbps
   at 1080p30 - and no H.264 profile was requested, so an MFT was free to
   pick Baseline (no CABAC, no 8x8 transform). Media Foundation's encoder
   is weaker than VideoToolbox at equal bitrate, and this app's output is
   its worst case: hard-edged pixel art, flat colour fields, dithering,
   fine generative detail. Raised to 0.30 bpp (cap 80 Mbps) and set High
   profile, best-effort so a refusing encoder still works.

   [file] was running on bare AVFoundation defaults with the same
   problem, less severely; it now uses the identical ladder plus High
   profile, so the two platforms agree by construction.

Not fixed here, and worth its own change: recording is a real-time
capture, not a render. CaptureFrame() runs once per rendered frame from
CookIfNeeded, and recordFps only stamps timestamps - it paces nothing -
so file duration is frameCount/recordFps regardless of how long those
frames took. The encoder queue is 4 deep and silently drops past that.
INFINITE_AUDIORECTEST already works around this, checking duration
against the real frame count rather than wall-clock elapsed time.

Verified: macOS hygiene suite 59 passed / 0 failed; INFINITE_VIDEOAUDIOTEST
round-trips and ffprobe reports profile=High. Frame drops in that fixture
are 37/18 both before and after, so the higher bitrate did not worsen
pacing.

Per windows-parity section 4, Windows CI cannot reach the recorder - it
proves the change links, nothing more. Both fixes need a real Windows
confirmation before being reported as verified.

subject: Fix eight Windows/parity defects and un-blind the hygiene gate
query_full:
Fix eight Windows/parity defects and un-blind the hygiene gate

The pillar-parity audit surfaced two test-harness holes and confirmed six
still-open defects from [file] against current source.

Test harness:

- [file] matched only FAIL|BUG$, but 56 fixture failure branches in
  [file] print a bare SUSPECT / MISMATCH / DID NOT MOVE / TONE MISSING.
  Every one of those failed silently with the gate reporting green. Widen the
  marker and, separately, require a positive verdict at all, so a fixture that
  dies before asserting can no longer pass by staying quiet. [file] gets the
  same two rules so the gates agree.

- Two failures the old gate was hiding, both found by the above:
  MACROTEST asserted the Macro XY pad against a size-x range of 0.01..0.50
  while the slider has been 0.01..1.0, so the pad - a core performance
  control - had been unverified for as long as the range has been wider.
  GEOTEST asserted LastUploads() == 0 on a steady frame, but that counter is
  reset inside Render3DNode's draw and the cache's ideal outcome is skipping
  the pass entirely, leaving the previous render's count in place. It read
  SUSPECT on a perfectly-behaving cache. Assert the frame-to-frame delta,
  which is the invariant actually meant.

Windows defects (1.3-1.8), all confirmed live before fixing:

- 1.3 MIDI clock sync never worked. HandleShortMessage masked status & 0xF0
  and then switched on 0xF8/0xFA/0xFC, which that mask cannot produce, so
  Pulse()/Reset() were dead code and MidiClockIsPresent() was permanently
  false. macOS tests the raw status first and syncs fine. Dispatch System
  Real-Time before masking.

- 1.6 Audio Analyze drove visuals wrongly. low/mid/high came from fixed band
  indices (~20-106 / ~106-373 / ~1982-4571 Hz vs macOS's 20-250 / 250-2000 /
  2000-16000), with low's weights summing to 1.5. Three further divergences
  found while fixing: bands[] used a linear clamp(v*4) against macOS's
  compressive sqrt(12v), the ladder stopped at 16 kHz where macOS runs to
  nyquist, and rms/peak/low/mid/high were never smoothed. Both paths run the
  same 1024-point FFT with the same normalisation, so all formulas are now
  transcribed from [file] and agree by construction.

- 1.8 Dropped notes with 2+ controllers. MidiStart opens every device with
  CALLBACK_FUNCTION, so the "single-producer" note ring had one producer per
  device racing the same index. Serialise on a dedicated ringMutex - not
  gState.mutex, which the Note Off path already holds when it publishes.

- 1.4 All Windows text rendered at the wrong size. The cap-height pass passed
  GGO_GLYPH_INDEX while asking for L'H', measuring glyph 72 instead of the
  letter. Also fixes letter spacing (applied in em units, then divided by cap
  height) and quadratic tessellation that never reached t=1.0, notching every
  on-curve point.

- 1.7 Camera frames sheared at unaligned widths. The file-decode path was
  fixed to read MF_MT_DEFAULT_STRIDE; the camera path still assumed w*4.

- 1.5 Upgrading macOS users silently lost their theme and recents when these

subject: Fix exported video drifting out of sync with live audio
query_full:
Fix exported video drifting out of sync with live audio

A live-audio recording has two independent clocks. The video track's PTS is
a plain frame counter over recordFps on both platforms - frameIndex/fps via
AVAssetWriter on macOS, FrameNumberToHns(frameCount, fps) via Media
Foundation on Windows - while live audio is stamped from the real captured
sample count. OutputNode::CaptureFrame emitted exactly one video frame per
*rendered* frame, so the file came out with a video duration of
renderedFrames/recordFps against an audio duration of real elapsed time.
Unless the render loop happened to hold exactly recordFps, the two walked
apart linearly across the take: 30s of audio recorded while rendering at
20fps produced 20s of video. Playback while monitoring is real-time either
way, which is why it looked fine in the app and only broke in the export.

Pace the video against the same sample count the muxer stamps the audio
with, using RecorderAppend's repeatCount - which both recorders already
honour and nothing had ever passed anything but 1 to. Rendering faster than
the target decimates, slower pads with a repeat, and the final drain takes
the whole remainder so the tail reaches the audio's full length. Deriving
the target from the audio sample count rather than a wall clock also keeps
it immune to the audio device clock drifting from the system clock, which
is its own source of desync over a long take.

Only the live path needs this: with an audio file source the recorders
slave audio to the video's synthetic clock instead, so that path is in sync
by construction and still keeps every rendered frame.

Also surface capture-ring overflow in the recording status - dropped audio
samples shift everything after the gap earlier in the file, so a stall that
costs audio is a sync bug, not just a glitch.

Add INFINITE_RECSYNCTEST, which simulates whole takes at render rates
above, below and equal to the target and asserts the video timeline tracks
the audio timeline to within a frame throughout. It is pure arithmetic over
the pacing both recorders' PTS depend on, so it runs in the hygiene gate and
on the Windows CI runner - the one place the Media Foundation half of this
can be executed by machine at all.

subject: Fix use-after-free crash: gate retired-node teardown on audio thread progress
query_full:
Fix use-after-free crash: gate retired-node teardown on audio thread progress

Undo (Cmd+Z) retires every node into gRetiredNodes and destroys them
unconditionally at the top of the next video frame - a delay sized only
for a GL-texture hazard, with no relationship to whether the real-time
audio thread has actually finished a block against the topology that
referenced them. Under load (e.g. synchronous sample decode during an
undo restore) the audio thread could still be mid-ProcessBlock on a
freed node, producing a SIGBUS wild-pointer crash inside
SpecBlurKernel::ProcessBlock.

AudioEngine now stamps each published topology with a monotonically
increasing generation and records the generation the audio thread has
actually finished processing. Retired nodes record the last generation
that could still reach them, and gRetiredNodes only drains an entry once
the audio thread confirms it has moved past that generation (or the
engine isn't running at all).

subject: Fix mp3/non-native-rate file playback speed and position display
query_full:
Fix mp3/non-native-rate file playback speed and position display

AudioFilePlayerAudioNode::ProcessBlock always advanced its read cursor
by exactly 1 frame per output sample, which only produces correct pitch
and speed when the decoded file's sample rate matches the audio
engine's running rate - e.g. a 44.1kHz mp3 played back on a 48kHz
device played fast and sharp. Steps the cursor by the file/engine rate
ratio instead, with linear interpolation between the two nearest
source frames since the cursor is now generally non-integral.

Also fixes PositionSeconds(), which divided the (now file-rate-based)
frame counter by the engine's sample rate rather than the file's -
would have shown an incorrect elapsed-time/progress-bar reading
whenever the two rates differ, even after the speed fix above.

subject: Fix undo/redo and delete stalls on large patches (Part A)

Fix undo/redo and delete stalls on large patches (Part A)

BuildPatchData() was O(N^2) from linear address->index lookups when
resolving cable endpoints; switched to reverse-lookup unordered_maps.
Undo/redo snapshots were deep-copied and every mouse click pushed a
full snapshot regardless of whether anything changed; snapshotting is
now gated on ed::GetHoveredNode()/selection, and Undo()/Redo() move
snapshots instead of copying. Multi-node delete rebuilt the whole audio
topology once per deleted node; it's now batched to once per delete op
via gDeferAudioRebuild. gUndoStack/gRedoStack changed from vector to
deque so front/back pop-and-discard doesn't shift the whole buffer.

Added a INFINITE_UNDOPERFTEST self-test (registered in the hygiene
driver as UNDOPERFTEST) that measures click/delete/group-delete/undo/
redo timings on a 300-node synthetic patch, and ScopedPerfTimer
instrumentation (gated on INFINITE_PERFTIMING) around BuildPatchData,
ApplyPatchData, and RebuildAudioTopology.

Measured before/after on a 300-node / 50-node-group-delete patch (no
file-backed assets, so this isolates the click/delete/snapshot fixes
rather than Part B's decode-cache work):

comparison against pristine main that all three failures

subject: Fix Offline Render audio speed and give duration real controls
query_full:
Fix Offline Render audio speed and give duration real controls

Two independent defects made a rendered take's audio play back off-speed
against its picture, both in the offline path only:

1. The take's audio was budgeted and muxed at a hardcoded 44100 Hz while
   the graph's AudioNodes stay PrepareToPlay'd at the live device's rate -
   a 48kHz device rendered as 44.1kHz is an 8.8% speed error. The rate is
   now read from the device before it is detached, threaded through
   StartOfflineRender, and used for both the per-frame sample budget and
   the muxer's declared rate. The per-frame budget also comes from a
   running cumulative target instead of a fixed round(sr/fps) quota, so an
   fps that doesn't divide the rate evenly can't drift, and a budget over
   kAudioMaxBlockFrames (any fps below ~12) is generated in several blocks
   instead of being silently truncated - truncation shortened the audio
   track, i.e. sped it up against the video.

2. The capture ring was armed before the audio device was detached, so the
   live callback kept writing into it during AVAudioEngine's teardown. The
   self-test take (1.0s of picture) came out with 1.33s of audio, all of it
   past that tail out of sync. The device is now stopped first and the ring
   drained before arming.

OFFLINERENDERTEST now asserts the appended sample count against
round(frames * rate / fps) and the movie duration against the take's own
length, rather than merely that an audio track exists - the assertion the
plan called for, and the one that catches both defects.

UI: duration and fps are typed InputInt fields (clamped) with 15/30/45/60s
presets and a live frame-count readout, replacing sliders that made an
exact value fiddly to hit. Offline Render also starts the audio device
briefly if a synth-audio take is requested while audio is off, since the
graph is only PrepareToPlay'd once a device has opened, and leaves it off
afterwards if it was off before.

subject: Fix offline render dropping frames and hanging on cancel
query_full:
Fix offline render dropping frames and hanging on cancel

Two defects behind the "rendered audio is sped up" report, both only
visible on takes long enough to back the encoder queue up:

- The encoder queue admits frames against a 256MB byte budget and drops
  what does not fit. That is right for a live take (better to lose a
  frame than to stall the UI) and catastrophic offline: a 60fps x 30s
  render landed 1221 of its 1800 frames, giving a 20.35s video track
  against a full 30.00s audio track. The offline pump now asks
  Platform::RecorderQueueHasRoom before rendering a frame and waits
  instead of handing over a frame that would be thrown away.

- Cancel routed through RecorderStop, which drains the whole backlog
  before returning, so it sat at "Finalizing..." for as long as
  finishing would have taken. Platform::RecorderCancel drops the queued
  frames, skips finalize, and removes the partial file: measured at 3
  main-loop frames on a queue deep enough to have taken hundreds.

MovieInfo now carries per-track durations, and the fixture asserts what
landed in the FILE rather than what was handed to the recorder - the
frame-drop bug passed every append-side assertion we had.

Sweep coverage for both: a 1800-frame take and a cancel on that same
deep queue.

subject: Fix offline render deadlocking against the writer's audio gate
query_full:
Fix offline render deadlocking against the writer's audio gate

A render with audio would stop dead a few dozen frames in and never
recover - the progress dialog frozen at 5-9%, Cancel the only way out.
Yesterday's backpressure fix is what made it visible: the pump now waits
for encoder room instead of letting the queue drop frames, and that wait
turned out to be one half of a deadlock.

Measured at the stall, not inferred: writer=writing, videoReady=0,
audioReady=1, audio track fully written, one frame queued, every encoder
thread idle, permanently. The same take renders to completion video-only.

AVAssetWriter will not take more video until the take's audio track has
run past the same point. A pump that stops rendering because the encoder
queue is full also stops generating the audio the writer is waiting for,
so the two sides wait on each other. Two fixes, both needed:

- While waiting for encoder room, keep generating audio, up to a second
  ahead of the picture (OfflineAudioFramesOwed takes a lookahead, capped
  at the take's own frame total so the audio track can never outrun it).
  This alone took the reproduction from frame 73 to frame 846 of 900.

- Close the audio track once its fixed budget is spent. The audio for a
  take finishes before the last frames are written, and the writer keeps
  holding video not-ready while it still expects audio - which is what
  the remaining 54 frames were waiting for.

Also here: an offline render now runs with vsync off and a 100ms pump
batch instead of 20ms against a vsync'd 16.7ms frame, so it is not
throttled to roughly half duty by the display; and the progress dialog
reports rate, ETA, "waiting for the encoder to catch up", and how long
it has been since the last frame - a long render and a wedged one used
to look identical.

INFINITE_OFFLINERENDER_QUEUEBYTES shrinks the encoder queue's byte
budget so the whole thing reproduces in seconds at fixture resolution
instead of needing a real 1080p patch; it is in the sweep as a fixture.
query_subject: Fix offline render deadlocking against the writer's audio gate

subject: Fix stereo-pair corruption in AudioCaptureRing on overflow/odd reads
query_full:
Fix stereo-pair corruption in AudioCaptureRing on overflow/odd reads

AudioCaptureRing::Write() dropped samples one at a time on overflow, so
a call that always hands it an even (L,R-paired) count could still
commit an odd number of trailing floats before the ring filled up.
Nothing re-anchors the stream's L/R phase afterward, so every pair
written after that point is silently channel-swapped - not shorter (the
existing duration/sample-count assertions never catch it), but garbled
until another odd-offset event happens to restore parity by chance.
Read() had the same class of bug from the consumer side for an odd
maxCount. This is a much better fit for a take reported as "sped up
initially, then completely breaks" (alternating noise and silence) than
a pure sample-count shortfall.

Both functions now only ever write/read whole stereo pairs, dropping or
holding back a trailing half-pair instead of committing/returning it
alone. Added INFINITE_AUDIORINGTEST, a deterministic headless
regression test that forces a mid-call overflow and an odd-sized read
and checks the ring never splits a pair - verified it fails against the
pre-fix code and passes against the fix. Also added
INFINITE_OFFLINERENDER_COOKDELAYMS to the offline render fixture to
simulate a heavy per-frame GPU cook (the condition the user's real
patch has that the existing fixture didn't), and wired both into the
av-sync-sweep driver.

[file] is shared cross-platform code ([file]),
so this fix applies to both macOS and Windows without a separate
Platform:: mirror.

subject: Fix Poisson Disk scatter tanking frame rate on Distribute Points on Faces
query_full:
Fix Poisson Disk scatter tanking frame rate on Distribute Points on Faces

The saturation break was scaled by the requested point count (cap * 30)
instead of being a fixed measure of local saturation, so a high-density
scatter burned up to 30x cap wasted candidate draws every rebuild - each
walking an unordered_map neighbour grid (heap alloc per new cell, hash +
pointer chase per lookup). Above cap ~66k the break was unreachable
entirely (saturationLimit exceeded the 2M candidate hard cap), so those
scatters burned the full budget every frame.

Fixes:
- saturationLimit is now a fixed 1500 consecutive rejects, independent
  of cap, and always well below the maxCandidates backstop.
- The unordered_map neighbour grid is replaced with a flat open-addressed
  table (gridKeys/gridHead) plus an intrusive per-point linked list
  (cellNext), sized off the accepted-point budget with no per-cell heap
  allocation.
- DistributePointsOnFacesNode now scatters once on the source mesh and
  transforms the result into each instance's space, instead of re-running
  the full Poisson search per instance (up to 256x).

Behaviour change: since the termination rule and per-instance seeding
both changed, an already-saved patch using Poisson mode or instancing
will reopen with a different point count/arrangement. This is unavoidable
for a correct fix.

Added a timing self-test (density 300 / minDistance 0.1 on a sphere,
must finish under 10ms) to DISTRIBUTETEST; the existing minDistance,
determinism, and saturation self-tests are unchanged and still pass.

subject: Fix note-on click in Oscillator and Wavetable
query_full:
Fix note-on click in Oscillator and Wavetable

Both nodes share WavetableSynthCore's voice path, whose polyphony
normalisation recounted `active` every sample and applied 1/sqrt(active)
directly. `active` is an integer, so the gain was a step function: any
note-on overlapping a sounding voice - a chord, or just the previous
note's release tail - moved it 1 -> 2 within one sample and snapped the
gain on the ALREADY-SOUNDING voice from 1.0 to 0.7071. That is a -3 dB
discontinuity in the output waveform (-6 dB with Chorder's 1 -> 4), and
the new note's attack cannot mask it because the step lands on the old
voice. It fired again in reverse whenever a tail went idle.

Ramp the gain through a persistent one-pole (15 ms, fixed - this is a
click fix, not a musical control, so it is deliberately not tied to the
glide knob) instead of applying it as a step. Initialised to 1.0 in
PrepareToPlay, not 0.0, or the first note would fade in. Steady state is
unchanged: the smoother settles on the same 1/sqrt(N).

Also make voice stealing click-free. On the all-busy steal path NoteOn
resets the stolen voice's phase and filter state while Envelope::NoteOn
deliberately keeps mLevel, so a fresh waveform was spliced in at the old
note's amplitude. Zero the amp envelope first, via a new explicit
Envelope::ResetLevel() called only from that path - NoteOn()'s no-reset
behaviour is load-bearing for legato and same-note retrigger and must
stay as it is.

Verified by two new DSPTEST checks in RunWavetableFixture:

- Continuity across an overlapping note-on. Note 1 sounds for 200 ms
  with a 4 s release, is released, and note 2 arrives while its tail is
  still loud. The scan is on the second difference, not the first: a
  level step adds to the waveform's own slew, so whether it reads as a
  spike in |x[n]-x[n-1]| depends on which way the waveform happened to
  be moving - the first-difference version of this check measured the
  real -3 dB step as 0.99x the steady slew and passed the broken code.
  The second difference has no such cancellation. Reverting the fix
  takes this from 1.03x to 32.6x its threshold.

- Steady-state loudness unchanged: a held 3-note chord's RMS matches
  1/sqrt(3) of the same three notes rendered solo and summed, to within
  0.01%.

run-infinite-hygiene: 62 passed. VIDEOAUDIOTEST and PLUGINDRAGTEST fail
in this worktree, but both fail identically when the main-built binary
is run from the same directory - environmental (no scanned VST3, movie
writer produces no tracks here), not a regression from this change.

subject: Fix glide/portamento: preserve pitch smoother on active voice repitch

Fix glide/portamento: preserve pitch smoother on active voice repitch

Bug fix: WavetableSynthCore NoteOn was calling SetImmediate() on every
new note (when v.note != note), which snapped the pitch smoother to the
target frequency instantly and defeated the glide parameter entirely.

This fixes the glide knob for OscillatorNode and WavetableNode in

Performance: hoist expf() glide coefficient computation out of per-voice
inner loops in EquationNode and WaveTerrainNode. The glide parameter
doesn't change within a single sample, so computing the coefficient once
per sample instead of once per voice per sample avoids redundant
transcendental function calls.

subject: fix(field): reduce.<op>(x) over a plain element-domain local read 0.0
query_full:
fix(field): reduce.<op>(x) over a plain element-domain local read 0.0

Element-domain reduce.<op>(x) - sum/mean/rms/min/max, the 1-arg form -
silently always returned 0.0 when x was an ordinary local (e.g. `wave =
sin(...); output frame float w = reduce.max(wave)`), even though the
compiler accepts this and its own error hint recommends exactly this
pattern. Root cause: only P/N/uv/Cd have per-element persistent storage
in ElementStore; a plain local only ever lived in ElementBackend's
transient per-iteration register map, which OpReduceElementAttrib's
ElementStore::GetAttribLane(name, lane) read could never see. The
shipped "Boundary Chime Sensor" preset ([file]) hit this
exactly and has likely always read a constant 0.0 chime output.

Fix, entirely in src/core/field/ (compile-time IR + the element
backend, no new backend-specific IR node or pointer-keyed side table):

- [file]/.h: when reduce.<op>(bareVar) is lowered and bareVar is
  Element-domain and not P/N/uv/Cd, register it into the
  ElementIRProgram's declaredAttribs list (ElementScope::
  MarkNeedsPersistentStorage) so ElementStore actually allocates a slot
  for it - ElementBackend's existing OpStoreAttrib codegen for a plain
  local's first assignment was already unconditional, it was just
  writing into a slot that never existed.
- A second, related bug this surfaced: such a reduce is domain-coarsened
  to Frame and would hoist into the prologue block, which runs BEFORE
  the element loop populates the target's buffer for the current cook -
  reading stale (or, on the first cook, still-zero) data instead of
  this cook's real values. Fixed by adding a third execution phase,
  postLoop (ElementIRProgram::postLoop / ElementProgram::postLoop),
  that runs once, after the element loop, for exactly the statements
  that need it - tracked via a new IRNode::reduceNeedsPostLoop flag set
  only for reduce over a non-P/N/uv/Cd bare name, so reduce(P) (etc.)
  keeps hoisting into the ordinary prologue exactly as before.
- [file]: added SECTION 17 to the INFINITE_FIELDELEMENTTEST
  harness - reduce.max over a plain local against a hand-computed
  expected max, plus the shipped Boundary Chime Sensor preset reading
  0.0 with nothing over threshold and ~1.0 once a vertex crosses it.

Verified: clean build; INFINITE_FIELDELEMENTTEST (new SECTION 17) OK;
re-ran every INFINITE_FIELD*TEST fixture (FIELDTEST, FIELDPARAMTEST,
FIELDSTATETEST, FIELDTRANSFERTEST, FIELDSAMPLETEST, FIELDPINDECLTEST) -
all OK, including FIELDTRANSFERTEST's existing reduce.mean(P) case,
which an earlier draft of this fix regressed by hoisting it into
postLoop unnecessarily; run-infinite-hygiene --fast, 21/21 green; the
geometry-transform-sweep driver, all sweeps green. The 3-arg
reduce.rms(in, lo, hi) form is untouched and doesn't need this fix -
[file]'s ValidateReduce accepts it only for Domain::Sample, a
different code path entirely (the sample-domain register machine, not
ElementBackend). No change to ParamMailbox, MeterRing, [file],
or [file].

subject: fix: snap-to-scale-then-clamp could leak out-of-key notes
query_full:
fix: snap-to-scale-then-clamp could leak out-of-key notes

Random Note Generator, Bouncing Balls, and CV to Pitch all snapped a
pitch to the current scale and then clamped the result into the
node's lo/hi range with a plain numeric clamp. The range boundary
itself isn't guaranteed to be in-scale, so a wandering note could get
shoved onto an out-of-key boundary note (e.g. C#4 while locked to C
major pentatonic).

Add MusicTime::SnapToScaleInRange, which searches inward from the
crossed boundary for the nearest in-scale note instead of clamping
blindly, and use it at all three call sites.

Fix knob gesture recording: trailing Dummy was eating the item state

KnobFloat and VFaderFloat both ended with ImGui::Dummy() to reserve the
full layout cell. Dummy is ItemSize *plus* ItemAdd(bb, 0), and that
ItemAdd overwrites g.LastItemData with a zero id - so every
IsItemActivated/IsItemActive/IsItemHovered that ModKnob runs after the
widget returns was querying the spacer, not the InvisibleButton.

whole post-draw block was dead: no undo checkpoint on grab, no
GestureRecorder::StopPlayback, and no NotifyMovement. Shift+drag never
opened a recording session, so IsRecording() stayed false and the red
tint from 2cc158a/69ec2f9 never had anything to show - on the EQ band
freq/Q/gain knobs and on every other ModKnob in the app. ModSlider's
identical block always worked because ImGui::SliderFloat leaves its own
item last; BipolarKnobFloat and the fader path used by Macro Knob/Slider
worked because they call the recorder internally, before the Dummy.

Dummy did and leaves the InvisibleButton's item data standing.

query_full:
fix(field): replace flawed noise generator, rework Piano and Bell synthesis

The multiplicative-congruential real-number recurrence used for noise
(seed = (seed*11035.152+0.12345)%1.0) short-cycled and correlated,
producing a tonal "screech" instead of broadband noise, which also
degraded every noise-dependent preset (snare, hi-hat, sweeper, crackle,
raindrops). Replaced with a standard sin-hash pseudo-random generator
across all five.

Acoustic Grand Piano used an exact 2x harmonic ratio and a per-sample
soft-saturator; real piano partials are stretched sharp of integer
ratios (inharmonicity), so the second partial now sits at 2.035x, and
the saturator was removed to free register budget for a hammer-noise
excitation "chiff" (the compiler's SSA-only allocator has no register
reuse and the original was already at 122/128 registers).

Crystalline Tubular Bell used arbitrary partial ratios (1, 2.76, 5.40),
which read as xylophone-like rather than bell-like. Replaced with the
named partials of real bell acoustics - prime, tierce (the
characteristic minor-third "bell" dissonance), and nominal (perceived
strike pitch/brightness) - trimmed to 3 partials to fit the register cap.

fix(field): retune noise-driven synth gain staging, rebuild foliage as clustered points

Sweeper's resonant filter had no output limiter at all, so its feedback
could ring well past +-1 - added one and trimmed the feedback amount.

transient and had no limiter on partial 1; scaled it down and restored
a soft limiter.

how the formula was tuned it could only ever read as a bumpy ball -
structurally the wrong technique for foliage. Rebuilt it the same way
the existing Flower/Pine Tree/Mushroom presets build organic detail:
Points topology with explicit golden-angle-placed clusters, each an
independent puffy blob, giving actual bonsai foliage pads instead of a
single lumpy sphere. Brilliant Cut Diamond's normal was a coarse
per-band constant instead of the true slanted facet-plane normal, so
lit facets barely differed from each other; computed the real pavilion/
crown/table plane normals so the facets actually catch light distinctly.

subject: fix(mesh): make RecalculateNormals flip actually reverse winding
query_full:
fix(mesh): make RecalculateNormals flip actually reverse winding

MeshOps::RecalculateNormals's flip=true path only negated the computed
normal vector; Mesh::indices winding was left untouched. Since the main
3D render shader does back-face culling with no gl_FrontFacing fixup,
flipping normals without reversing winding didn't invert the surface —
it just lit the same visible faces from behind, going black. (The node
mini-viewport shader does have a gl_FrontFacing fixup, so preview and
final render disagreed on any flipped mesh.)

Fix: when flip is true, also reverse each triangle's winding — swap the
2nd/3rd vertex in out.indices in the smooth (shared-vertex) path, and
emit the three expanded vertices in reversed order in the flat
(unshared-vertex) path. The winding reversal happens after normals are
computed from the original winding, and the already-negated normal is
exactly what the reversed winding would itself produce, so the two stay
consistent — orientation is genuinely inverted, matching Blender's Flip
Normals.

[file]'s Displace and Wrap ops both call
MeshOps::RecalculateNormals directly for their own flipNormals handling
(no duplicated flip logic), so they pick up the fix automatically.
query_subject: fix(mesh): make RecalculateNormals flip actually reverse winding

subject: fix(mesh): weld duplicate vertices when accumulating smooth normals
query_full:
fix(mesh): weld duplicate vertices when accumulating smooth normals

Root cause: MeshOps::RecalculateNormals's smooth path accumulated face
normals through the raw, unwelded `indices` array. Every primitive in
this codebase duplicates vertices at UV seams and hard edges (PushGrid
gives Cube(1) 24 vertices for 8 corners, see the comment near
BuildWeldMap's caller), so each duplicate only ever accumulated its own
single face normal. On a cube, where every vertex belongs to exactly
one face, that made smooth normals identical to flat normals -
the Normals node with "flat shade" off appeared to do nothing. On a UV
sphere/cylinder the seam vertices were never averaged with their
duplicates, producing a visible normal seam and a wrong-reading
cylinder cap rim.

Fix: accumulate face normals per weld-group representative (via
BuildWeldMap(in), the same helper and pattern MeshOps::Smooth already
uses for vertex positions), normalize per representative, then copy
each representative's normal back out to every vertex in its group.
Geometry itself is not welded - vertex count and positions are
unchanged, only the normal each duplicate reports is now shared with
its coincident neighbors. This also composes correctly with the flip
option: winding/flip is applied per accumulated normal exactly as
before, so a flipped-winding mesh still welds and flips consistently.

Explicit judgement call: no angle threshold / auto-smooth option was
added. `flat shade` is already the "keep every edge hard" answer, and
a threshold would introduce a parameter this node doesn't currently
expose.

Verified: full rebuild is clean, and
[file] passes all sweeps.
query_subject: fix(mesh): weld duplicate vertices when accumulating smooth normals

subject: fix(blend): weight blend result by backdrop alpha, fix output-alpha compositing
query_full:
fix(blend): weight blend result by backdrop alpha, fix output-alpha compositing

[file] and [file] both mixed the blend-mode result
directly against unpremultiplied a.rgb/acc.rgb and combined alpha with
max(a.a, b.a). Where the backdrop was transparent, blendMode() was fed
whatever colour sat under alpha 0 (usually black), so Multiply/Darken/
Burn etc. produced black fringes around transparent edges. And max()
alpha meant stacking two 50% layers gave 0.5 instead of the correct
0.75.

Replaced both compositing steps with the standard source-over formula:
  as = source coverage (uMix * b.a in BlendNode; amt = uOpacity*layer.a
       in LayerStackNode)
  cs = mix(source.rgb, blended, backdrop.a)   -- mode degrades to Normal
       as the backdrop's alpha goes to 0
  ar = as + backdrop.a * (1 - as)
  cr = (cs*as + backdrop.rgb*backdrop.a*(1-as)) / ar, guarded for ar~0

Verified algebraically that for the common opaque-over-opaque case
(a.a == b.a == 1, uMix == 1 / amt == 1) this reduces to exactly the old
behaviour: cs collapses to `blended`, ar collapses to 1, and cr
collapses to `blended` -- bit-identical to the previous
mix(a.rgb, blended, uMix*b.a) / max(a.a,b.a) result. So every existing
patch blending two fully-opaque layers is unaffected; only partially
transparent backdrops/layers change (correctly).

Erase branches (uMode/uModes[i] == kEraseMode) are untouched in both
files, per the bug report -- Erase's current alpha-only behaviour is
correct.

Cleanup: replaced the magic number 30 with BlendModes::kEraseMode in
both shader-string erase checks.

Did not hoist a shared composite GLSL snippet into [file]: the
two call sites use different variable names and control flow (a/b pair
with an early erase early-return vs. an accumulator loop with
continue), so sharing would need an awkward macro/snippet with several
parameters and wouldn't meaningfully reduce duplication. Fixed both
copies independently instead.

Build verified clean via cmake --build build.
query_subject: fix(blend): weight blend result by backdrop alpha, fix output-alpha compositing

subject: fix(3d): correct Join Geometry vertex-colour merge and keep per-input colour
query_full:
fix(3d): correct Join Geometry vertex-colour merge and keep per-input colour

JoinGeometryNode::Rebuild's kMerge branch only appended placed.vertexColor
when non-empty, without padding to placed.vertices.size()*3 for inputs that
lacked vertex colour. That misaligned colour data with vertex indices
whenever a colourless input preceded a coloured one (and usually silently
dropped colour entirely once Mesh::HasVertexColor()'s size check failed).
It also meant a merged mesh always rendered with one material/colour
(materialFrom's), so e.g. a red sphere merged with a yellow cube came out
entirely red.

Fix always appends exactly one colour triple per vertex per input: the
input's own placed.vertexColor when well-formed, otherwise a fill of that
input's material albedo (Material::color). This keeps mCache.vertexColor
index-aligned with mCache.vertices and lets each merged part keep its own
colour via the existing aVertexColor render path.

Adds a new "keep input colours" bool param (default on) next to "material
from input" so merge can still reproduce the old single-material look when
turned off. Registered in VisitParams for save/load, and tracked in the
node's dirty-check (mBuiltKeepInputColours) so toggling it triggers a
rebuild.

Verified with geometry-transform-sweep's [file] (all sweeps pass).

subject: Fix Join Geometry merge discarding a downstream Material's colour
query_full:
Fix Join Geometry merge discarding a downstream Material's colour

Two independent defects, both in JoinGeometryNode's merge path.

1. Manufactured vertex colour. The merge filled Mesh::vertexColor from
   each input's material albedo unconditionally, even when every input was
   colourless. vertexColor and Material::color are two independent inputs
   to the same shader product (base = uBaseColor * vInstanceColor *
   vVertexColor), but only vertexColor travels inside the mesh, and
   nothing downstream can tell manufactured filler apart from authored
   colour. So `join -> material(red) -> join -> render` rendered the inner
   join's manufactured white and ignored the Material entirely - the outer
   join saw HasVertexColor() and took the "input already has colour"
   branch. The merge now bakes colour only when there is real colour to
   preserve: some input carries authored vertexColor or per-instance
   colour, or the inputs' albedos actually differ. When it does bake, it
   bakes each input's absolute colour and GetMaterial() reports a neutral
   albedo, so the shader product reproduces each part exactly instead of
   tinting every part by whichever input materialFrom points at.
   Regression from d135d88, shipped in v0.3.4.

2. Invisible material invalidation. The dirty check tracked MeshRevision,
   matrices, instancers, mode and keepInputColours - not the input
   materials it was baking. IGeometrySource has no MaterialRevision(), and
   MaterialNode::MeshRevision() forwards its input's stamp verbatim, so a
   colour change upstream of a merge could never invalidate the baked
   colours; dragging the picker moved nothing at all. Input albedo is now
   part of the dirty check (mBuiltAlbedos), and the per-input GetMaterial()
   calls are fetched once per rebuild rather than three times, since joins
   nest and that walk multiplies at every level.

Adds COLOURSWEEPTEST: a probe source with a fixed material feeds every
geometry-consuming node type and asserts none of them invent vertexColor
for a colourless mesh, plus three targeted Join checks including the exact
reported patch. Reverting either fix fails it.
query_subject: Fix Join Geometry merge discarding a downstream Material's colour

subject: fix(mod): stop ModSliderInt from stomping expression/recording writes
query_full:
fix(mod): stop ModSliderInt from stomping expression/recording writes

ModSliderInt reseeded its backing proxy float from the node's *value
every frame unless Modulation::IsModulated() was true, but IsModulated
only detects a wired modulation cable - it doesn't see an active
expression or gesture/mod-recorder playback driving the same param.
Since the UI draw pass runs before ApplyModulationAndPalette applies
those each frame, any expression/recording write got stomped by the
next frame's reseed before the audio thread ever saw it, so params
driven this way (e.g. NoteSwitcherNode's manual slot) appeared frozen
while a wired LFO on the same control worked fine.

ModKnobInt already had the correct fix for this, for an unrelated
reason (it needs to preserve its drag accumulator across frames): it
tracks the last value it wrote back itself and only reseeds when
*value changed for some other reason. That guard is source-agnostic -
cable, expression, or recording all look the same to it - so porting
it into ModSliderInt fixes the shared helper for every caller at once,
including SwitcherNode's and Switcher3DNode's manual-slot sliders,
which had the identical latent bug.

fix(gesture-recorder): freeze looping recordings on spacebar pause

Gesture-recorded playback timestamped and replayed itself against

even after pausing the global transport with spacebar. Every other

subject: fix(vst3-scan): stop macOS batch scanner from over-blocklisting plugins
query_full:
fix(vst3-scan): stop macOS batch scanner from over-blocklisting plugins

The macOS batch-scan retry loop in ProbeVST3BundlesBatch never removed
already-described bundles from the retry list, had no iteration cap, and
relied solely on a dispatch_once-gated sentinel check to attribute a crash
to an offending bundle. A single crashing/slow plugin could therefore spin
the same batch indefinitely or silently fail to get attributed within one
scan, causing legitimate plugins to accumulate onto the persisted blocklist
across app relaunches ("most of my VSTs are blocklisted").

Port the three safeguards the Windows implementation already has: drop
successfully-described bundles from the retry list each pass (forward
progress), cap total iterations, and directly blocklist the front bundle
when a crash pass describes nothing at all.
query_subject: fix(vst3-scan): stop macOS batch scanner from over-blocklisting plugins

subject: fix(plugins-panel): stop iterator invalidation when removing a VST3 search folder
query_full:
fix(plugins-panel): stop iterator invalidation when removing a VST3 search folder

The "VST3 search folders" list in the Plugins panel iterated

or copy-first idiom already used for the same pattern in the Samples and
Media library panels.

subject: Fix MOLDERTEST determinism false-positive; document reconstruction gap
query_full:
Fix MOLDERTEST determinism false-positive; document reconstruction gap

The "same seed/generation diverged" failure was a fixture bug, not a
MolderDsp::Mutate/Rng bug: it memcmp'd the whole MolderDsp::Genome struct,
which ends in a trailing bool and therefore has compiler-inserted padding
that no constructor ever initializes. Two logically-identical Genomes could
differ in that uninitialized padding. Replaced the memcmp with an explicit
field-by-field comparison.

The "-6.7dB reconstruction error" failure is a real, already-investigated
gap in the additive resynthesis (dense-harmonic mainlobe overlap), not a
stale threshold — left open and documented rather than fixed or papered
over, since closing it needs real per-harmonic overlap compensation. Added
a "Known pre-existing failures" section to [file]
(its driver has no known-failure baseline mechanism, unlike
run-infinite-hygiene) plus a forward-looking cross-reference in
[file].

subject: fix(ui): correct Windows DPI scaling and add manual UI Scale override
query_full:
fix(ui): correct Windows DPI scaling and add manual UI Scale override

On Windows, GLFW window coordinates are physical pixels and
glfwGetWindowContentScale() reports the actual OS/monitor DPI factor, unlike
macOS where it's Retina-only sharpness info. The font block baked glyphs at
baseSize*xscale and then divided the same xscale back out via
FontGlobalScale, cancelling exactly and pinning text to a fixed 15 physical
px regardless of Windows display scaling (150%/200% had no effect on 4K).
ImGuiStyle::ScaleAllSizes() was also never called, so widget metrics never
scaled either.

Windows now bakes the font directly at baseSize*xscale with
FontGlobalScale=1 and calls ScaleAllSizes(xscale), so both text and widget
metrics track the monitor's DPI setting. macOS keeps its existing
Retina-aware math unchanged. Also adds a persisted gUiScale manual multiplier
(Appearance tab, "UI Scale" slider, requires restart) on top of the OS scale,
stored in Infinite.appearance as ui.scale=. Moved CategoryColors::LoadPreference()
earlier in startup, before the font/DPI block, since the override must be
known before the font atlas is baked.

Fixes #21

subject: fix: keep windows.h out of main.cpp; baseline the x86_64 metaball weld failure
query_full:
fix: keep windows.h out of main.cpp; baseline the x86_64 metaball weld failure

Adding [file] to [file] broke the Windows build in
a place nowhere near the include. On _WIN32 that header pulls [file]
and so <[file]>, and [file] declares a FUNCTION named Polyline,
which hides [file]'s global `struct Polyline` - so every MeshOps
declaration taking a `const Polyline&` stopped naming a type and MSVC
emitted a wall of errors pointing at [file]. [file] had included no
Windows header at all before this, which is why that struct has been safe
for years.

The helper was not needed: the window-icon branch is Linux-only (Windows
takes SetWindowIconFromResource, macOS takes neither), and on Linux a
path is already UTF-8, so a plain std::ifstream is correct. Comment at
the call site explains why not to reach for the portable helper here.

This was hidden behind the scanner link error - Infinite depends on the
scanner target, so while that failed to link, [file] was never compiled.
Fixing one revealed the other.

PHASECTEST is a different animal and is baselined, not fixed: its metaball
watertightness check reports 8 open edges on x86_64 and 0 on arm64 from an
identical 6096-triangle mesh, because BuildWeldMap compares float positions
against an epsilon that x86_64 codegen moves them across. Nothing in the
port touches [file]. It is real and user-visible - a non-watertight blob
renders shattered under backface culling, and every x86_64 user is on the
failing side - so the baseline entry carries the whole story and says to
remove it with a fix in BuildWeldMap, not before P5.

Both traps are now in linux-parity §3.6 and §3.7, along with the rule the
second one really teaches: local green on arm64 is not green.

subject: fix(mesh): make metaball edge lerp order-independent, fixing x86_64 weld
query_full:
fix(mesh): make metaball edge lerp order-independent, fixing x86_64 weld

MeshOps::BuildWeldMap already quantised positions to an integer grid before
hashing - that part was sound. The actual x86_64-only defect was upstream in
EmitTetra's lerpPoint ([file]): two tetrahedra sharing an edge each
classify their own corners into inside[]/outside[], so the same grid edge
could be lerped as (a, b) from one tetrahedron and (b, a) from its neighbour.
Those two expressions are mathematically equal but not bit-identical, and

subject: fix(arrange): force real redraw of geometry lanes during offline export
query_full:
fix(arrange): force real redraw of geometry lanes during offline export

CompositeArrangeTimelineVideo composites geometry-source clips through
NodeViewport's cached mini-viewport render. NodeViewport::Render is a
live-preview change-gate meant for UI glances - it skips re-rendering
and returns the prior frame's texture whenever the node's own
mesh/model/material/camera/instancing/texture revisions haven't ticked.
The offline export pump never signaled otherwise, so it recaptured
identical pixels under a correct-but-stale timestamp whenever a
geometry clip's revision counters happened not to tick between two
consecutive export frames, showing up as stutter/duplicate frames.

Pass Transport::Instance().IsOfflineMode() as NodeViewport::Render's
existing (previously unused at this call site) forceRedraw argument so
every offline-exported frame gets a real redraw. Live preview callers
(gNodeViewports) are untouched.
query_subject: fix(arrange): force real redraw of geometry lanes during offline export

subject: fix(arrange): also force redraw of Render3DNode's scene cache offline

fix(arrange): also force redraw of Render3DNode's scene cache offline

Render3DNode::CookIfNeeded has its own live-preview change-gate
(BuildSceneSignature() equality) that skips the shadow/opaque/
transmissive passes and reuses mColorTex whenever nothing it tracks
changed since the last cook. This is the same bug shape as the
already-fixed NodeViewport cache, but on the path arrangement clips
take when the assigned node is Render3DNode itself (or anything
downstream of it) rather than a raw IGeometrySource - CompositeArrange
TimelineVideo's else-branch reads GetOutputTexture() directly and
trusts whatever this cache last produced.

The signature isn't wrong, just insufficient for offline export's
guarantee: some upstream revisions don't tick on every export frame
(e.g. ParticleSystemNode's fixed-step accumulator, or an animated
albedo-only texture that BuildSceneSignature's texturedMaterial check
doesn't scan), so two adjacent export frames can hash identical and
silently recapture the prior frame's pixels under a new timestamp.

Add !Transport::Instance().IsOfflineMode() to the skip condition so a
take always redraws, mirroring the NodeViewport::Render forceRedraw
fix instead of duplicating its own bypass mechanism.

path (a value would snap to the click position for one frame before the
text box opened), and hover-to-type could steal keystrokes from any other
focused widget since it only checked "not this slider", not "nothing else
active". Both are fixed by deferring a fresh click's activation until it's
known whether a second click, a real drag, or neither follows, and by
gating hover-to-type on no widget anywhere holding ActiveId.

Also closes a gap in ArrangeContentEqual: pan/pitch/opacity/color-grade/
retrigger were missing from the gesture-undo content diff, so dragging
those sliders changed the live value but pushed no undo entry and never
marked the patch dirty.

Clip::retrigger existed in the model, was serialized, and had a UI
dropdown, but nothing in the audio engine ever read it - Timeline
(Continuous) and Retrigger on Enter were audibly identical. Wires it up:
AudioNode gets a RequestRetrigger() hook (AudioFilePlayerAudioNode reuses
its existing Restart request), AudioTerminal carries the clip's source
node, and RunTopology gets a lookahead pass that seeks the node before it
cooks a block whose span crosses a retrigger window's start. When a
node is shared across more than one lane, retrigger is suppressed for
those clips (falls back to continuous) rather than let two lanes fight
over one playback position, and the Clip Settings panel shows why.

subject: fix(linux): add reverse-playback frame cache to MediaLinux's decoder
query_full:
fix(linux): add reverse-playback frame cache to MediaLinux's decoder

INFINITE_VIDEOSPEEDTEST was failing because every single-frame reverse
or fast-scrub step triggered a full av_seek_frame + avcodec_flush_buffers
on MediaLinux's decode thread - the thread's jumpedBackward check fires
on every step during reverse playback since the target position keeps
moving behind the last delivered frame.

Initially suspected a Linux-specific GOP misconfiguration (a 2-second
GOP meant a short test clip could have only one keyframe). Shrinking
gop_size to fps/4 was tested and disproved that: the x264 log confirmed
the encoder config changed (keyint 7 vs 60, 9 I-frames vs 1), but
FrameUpdateCount got *worse*, not better - the dominant cost is the
seek/flush itself, not redecode distance from the nearest keyframe.
Reverted the GOP change.

Checked what macOS does for the same problem: [file] already has a
purpose-built reverse-playback frame cache (kReverseLookbackSeconds,
frameCache, PushCacheFrame/TryUseCache) with a comment describing this
exact stutter ("too small and reverse stutters on a rebuild almost
every frame"). Windows's [file] has no equivalent and reseeks on
every backward step same as Linux did, but gets away with it via
Media Foundation's hardware-accelerated seek. This confirms a reverse-
frame cache is a genuine, already-proven cross-platform requirement for
a software decoder, not a Linux-only quick fix - so this ports macOS's
existing design rather than inventing new architecture:

- VideoHandle gains a `frameCache` (FIFO by pts, capped at 256MB).
- Every frame VideoFrameAt delivers (forward or backward) is cached.
- VideoFrameAt serves a request from the cache when the ready queue has
  nothing new for it, before ever touching the decode thread.
- VideoThreadMain skips the seek entirely when a backward jump is
  already covered by the cache, and on a real backward seek, seeks
  kReverseLookbackSeconds behind the target (not exactly to it) so the
  frames decoded on the way there repopulate the cache and buy several
  more reverse steps before the next real seek.

Verified via 3 consecutive runs in the Xvfb/Docker environment:
FrameUpdateCount for reverse went from 3-8/60 to 24-30/60, forward from
0-5/60 to 13-60/60, both now clearing the >30 threshold every run.
VIDEOAUDIOTEST and RECEXPORTTEST re-confirmed unaffected (still pass).

Updates [file]: both VIDEOAUDIOTEST and
VIDEOSPEEDTEST are fixed, no longer P3 gaps.
query_subject: fix(linux): add reverse-playback frame cache to MediaLinux's decoder

subject: Fix cache budget, audio cursor, clip-bounce scope and Windows media type
query_full:
Fix cache budget, audio cursor, clip-bounce scope and Windows media type

Follow-ups to cae4444, from a review of that commit.

[file] - the scrub frame cache no longer being cleared on seek is what
makes scrubbing cheap, but it also means each handle now grows to its ceiling
and stays there. The 512 MB cap was per handle, so a four-clip project would
have sat on 2 GB of decoded frames. It is now one budget for the whole app,
with handles registered so eviction takes the globally least-recently-used
frame. That makes the cache shared state, and video decoding is not
single-threaded (ArrangeMediaImport opens a dropped clip and pulls its first
frame on a worker), so the registry, the clock and every frameCache touch are
behind a mutex. Also: a per-handle entry ceiling so the linear LRU scans stay
cheap for small frames; kReverseLookbackSeconds is used again rather than a
literal, and its comment now describes the 0.5s the code actually does; the
nearest-frame cache fallback no longer serves a frame up to 25 ms AHEAD of
the request; and the no-frame-produced path no longer records readerPts at a
position the reader is not at, which made the next call resume forward
decoding from the wrong place.

AudioEngine - the retrigger pass walked its cursor to numWindows once the
playhead passed the last clip and stored it there. The render pass reads that
as out of range and restarts at 0, so every block after the last clip paid a
full forward walk of the lane - the opposite of the O(1) the cursor exists
for. Clamped before storing.

[file] - "Bounce / Render Clip" bounded its range to the selected clips but
scoped output by lane, so another clip sharing that lane inside the range was
rendered into the bounce. Added a clip scope alongside the lane scope, honored
by the audio scheduler, the video collector and the live-source refusal sweep
(which would otherwise refuse a bounce over a camera on a clip it was not
rendering). A builder that resolves no clips now leaves an empty range and
fails visibly instead of writing four beats of silence.

The render dialog's source logic moved out of popup lambdas into
ArrangeRenderEffectiveAudioSource / ArrangeRenderEffectiveVideoSource, because
ARRANGERENDERTEST's section E was asserting against a private copy of the
logic cae4444 deleted - it kept passing while the shipping behaviour changed.
E now drives the shipping helpers, and a new E2 covers the clip scope. Removed
the code the dropdowns left stranded (sArrangeRenderCanvasUid,
ArrangeRenderCollectOutputNodes, the unreachable canRender clauses) and marked
Settings::renderAudioSource/renderVideoSource deprecated - they are still
serialized for file-format compatibility but nothing reads them.

[file] - MF_MT_YUV_MATRIX was being set on inType, which is
MFVideoFormat_RGB32 and has no YUV matrix. SetInputMediaType can reject the
unexpected attribute, and the SUCCEEDED(hr) chain would then abort recorder
setup silently. Dropped from inType; outType keeps it, and inType keeps the
full-range tag that tells the converter what our RGB is.

Verified: builds clean, hygiene fast tier 30/30, video/media/ui groups pass.
RECEXPORTTEST, AUDIOLIFECYCLETEST and AUDIORECOVERYTEST fail identically on
main in this session - no audio device available (CoreAudio -10875).

subject: Fix Sample split waveform/seek with a source-offset field
query_full:
Fix Sample split waveform/seek with a source-offset field

A split Sample clip's right half kept srcUid but had no way to know
where in the source file its own audio actually starts, so its static
waveform restretched the whole decoded file across its rect (showing
the file's start again instead of continuing the left half's shape)
and AudioEngine's retrigger/seek math always seeked relative to the
file's own beginning.

Add Clip::sourceOffsetSeconds (Sample-only): how far into the decoded
source buffer a clip's audio starts. Split() derives it for the right
half from the cut point converted ticks -> seconds via the clip's own
sampleBpm (tempo-invariant by construction). CarveRange - the same
implicit-split shape used by PlaceOverwrite and DuplicateBlock - gets
the identical treatment for both its "strictly contains" and "overlaps
right edge" cases.

Plumb the field through ClipWindow ([file]/.cpp) so the exact-
seek lookahead folds it into elapsedSeconds before the existing pitch/
tempo-ratio scaling, and through ArrangeComputeSampleStaticWave ([file])
so the static-waveform cache slices peaks to a clip's own sub-range of
the decoded file instead of the whole thing - triggered at import time
(offset 0) and now also at both Split call sites via the new
ArrangeRefreshSampleStaticWave helper.

Audit: TrimEdge/TrimGroupEdge share the same start-edge-moves shape but
are out of this fix's scope - flagged as a follow-up task rather than
folded in here.

subject: fix(arrange): sync Sample static waveform cache and unsynced clip length to live tempo
query_full:
fix(arrange): sync Sample static waveform cache and unsynced clip length to live tempo

The static waveform cache (ArrangeComputeSampleStaticWave) always inverted
the synced-clip length formula (TicksToSeconds(length, sampleBpm)) even for
unsynced clips, so it sliced the wrong sub-range of the decoded source file
the moment sync was off - the drawn waveform no longer matched what was
actually audible. Added SampleClipWindowSeconds() as the exact inverse of
SampleClipLengthTicks, branching on syncToTempo the same way, and wired
ArrangeRefreshSampleStaticWave() into every UI site that edits sync/Sample
BPM so the cache never goes stale.

Also: an unsynced clip's length only ever tracked explicit edits to the
Sample BPM field, never a live change to the global project tempo - so
turning off sync and then adjusting the transport BPM (rather than the
per-clip field) still visibly grew/shrank the clip's rendered length even
though nothing about the clip itself changed. Added
ArrangeResyncUnsyncedSampleLengths(), polled once per frame alongside the
existing ArrangePollMediaImports(), which recomputes length + refreshes the
static wave for every unsynced Sample clip when the live tempo moves.

Root cause of "Sample BPM edit does nothing while sync is off": Rebuild-
AudioTopology forced ClipWindow::sampleBpm to 0 whenever syncToTempo was
false, which permanently locked RunTopology's tempoRatioLive to 1.0
(native speed) regardless of the Sample BPM field. Fixes it with a new
frozen Clip::origBpm (captured once at import, never touched by later
edits) as the reference point: synced clips keep the existing bpm/
sampleBpm ratio, unsynced clips now use sampleBpm/origBpm - tempo-
independent, but reacting to the Sample BPM field like it always should
have. origBpm round-trips through Patch (new cliporigbpm tag, migrated
from sampleBpm for old patches) and is now compared in ArrangeContentEqual
so BPM/sync edits aren't silently dropped from undo.

Also fixes a real bug behind the user's "it's still sourcing from the
canvas node" intuition: a pasted/duplicated Sample clip kept the original
clip's srcUid, so two clips could contend over one node's single WSOLA
stretcher/cursor. ArrangeRespawnCloneNode now gives every pasted/
duplicated Sample clip (audio, video, or image) its own hidden
(hiddenFromCanvas) node and kicks a fresh decode of the same file,
tracked via a new ArrangePendingImport::isClone flag so the clone's
already-correct sampleBpm/origBpm/length aren't re-estimated and
overwritten when the decode lands. Split's two halves are left sharing
one node since they never play simultaneously on the same lane.

WsolaStretcher was already extracted to its own shared header
([file], prior commit) so this and the canvas
AudioFilePlayerAudioNode use the exact same stretch algorithm.

ArrangeComputeSampleStaticWave always used the synced-only

state. That formula is only mathematically consistent with the synced ratio
(liveBpm/sampleBpm); for an unsynced clip the actual playback ratio is
sampleBpm/origBpm, entirely independent of live tempo, so the displayed
waveform did not correspond to what was actually audible - editing Sample
BPM on an unsynced clip looked like it did nothing even though the rate
override was in fact changing.

Added an unsynced branch that derives windowSeconds from the box's own
live-tempo duration times the sampleBpm/origBpm ratio, matching
AudioEngine::RunTopology's formula exactly. Also updated the two stale
Sample BPM field comments (context menu and docked Clip Settings panel)
that still claimed sync-off means "no rate override applies" - the ratio
fix from the previous commit was already live there, only the comment was
wrong.

subject: fix(gesture-recorder): capture shift-drag gestures while transport is paused
query_full:
fix(gesture-recorder): capture shift-drag gestures while transport is paused

GestureRecorder timestamped both recording and playback off the same
clock, which the previous fix (0eb00b5) made freeze while the transport
is paused so a looping recording would hold still on pause. Side effect:
recording a new gesture while paused stamped every sample with the same
frozen time, so the trace had no duration and played back as a static
value instead of the drag that was just performed.

Split it into two clocks - the playback clock (unchanged, still freezes
on pause) and a new record clock that always advances regardless of
play state. NotifyMovement/MaybeFinishArmedRecording now timestamp
against the record clock, so shift+drag captures real motion whether
the transport is playing or paused; BeginFrame/GetPlaybackValue still
use the playback clock so looping recordings still freeze on pause.
