subject: fix(arrange): inspector fields type like the canvas ones, in their own units
query_full:
fix(arrange): inspector fields type like the canvas ones, in their own units

Four complaints, one cause: the Arrange inspector grew its own field
widgets instead of reusing the behaviour the canvas params already had.

1. Typing needed a backspace first. ImGui's TempInput path opens the box
   on the OLD text, and whether the keystroke that opened it replaces
   that text or lands beside it depends on frame ordering - so "0.3"
   over "0.80" came out wrong. The canvas has not had this problem since
   HandleParamTypeHotkeys: it seeds the box with exactly the typed
   character and puts the cursor after it. Same approach here, in one
   shared ArrangeTypedEdit used by every inspector field, with
   double-click and Ctrl+click still opening on the current value
   selected (there the intent is "replace all of it").

2. Typing '0' bypassed the clip. '0' is ArrangeToggleEnabledSelection,
   and the shortcut block's only guard was WantTextInput - which is
   still false on the frame a hover+type OPENS a field. Hovering a value
   field now arms ArrangeFieldHot() and suppresses every single-key
   timeline shortcut for that frame and the next, since the panel's key
   handling and the inspector draw in that order. The pointer sitting on
   a field is the statement that the next keystroke is a value.

3. Start/Length could not be typed at all - the bar.beat.sixteenth text
   is a literal, so the field carried ImGuiSliderFlags_NoInput and
   ctrl+click did nothing. They now accept "9.3.3", "9.3" or "9"
   through ArrangeParsePos, and lengths through a new ArrangeParseLen -
   the same text one index lower, because "1.0.0" is one bar where
   "1.1.1" is bar one. Two parsers, deliberately: reading a length with
   the position parser is a whole bar out.

4. Fades are milliseconds now, in both display modes. A fade is an
   envelope, not a place in the song; at 120 BPM a 20 ms fade is a sixth
   of a sixteenth, which the old bar.beat.sixteenth field could not
   express at all.

Both copies of these fields - the docked inspector and the right-click
menu - now call the same ArrangeTickField / ArrangeSliderFloat /
ArrangeDragFloat, rather than the menu keeping a second lambda that had
already drifted. Sample BPM was the last raw ImGui::DragFloat and goes
through ArrangeDragFloat too.

INFINITE_CLIPFIELDTEST covers the pure half: position round-trips
through the text the field shows, lengths differ from positions by
exactly one index, 20 ms lands under a sixteenth, the shortcut guard
arms and expires on the right frames, and Time mode moves Start/Length
to seconds while leaving fades in ms.

subject: Fix Analog sub oscillator emitting DC instead of a sub-octave tone
query_full:
Fix Analog sub oscillator emitting DC instead of a sub-octave tone

The sub osc read osc1's phase scaled by 0.5 and squared it against a
0.5 threshold. PolyBlepOsc::phase is 0..1, so the scaled value never
left [0, 0.5) and the comparison never flipped: subSample was a
constant +1.0. Scaling a phase compresses its range, it does not halve
its rate - the inverse trick works for sync (kWarpSync multiplies the
phase up and re-wraps) but cannot work downward.

The knob therefore injected raw DC into the pre-filter mix, biasing the
tanh drive stage and, in the free-running path, leaving a standing
offset on the output. No sub-octave tone at any setting.

Give the sub its own PolyBlepOsc, as WavetableSynthCore and the
FieldSynth presets already do, running at half osc1's post-FM pitch and
pre-unison-detune, so the sub does not beat against itself in the
register where beating is least wanted. Symmetric square (pw fixed at
0.5), BLEP'd like the other oscillators. Reset alongside the osc phases
in Voice::Reset and the free-running reset.

Both the free-running and the poly voice paths carried the bug.
query_subject: Fix Analog sub oscillator emitting DC instead of a sub-octave tone

subject: Fix the cutoff knob being greyed out on the comb filter types
query_full:
Fix the cutoff knob being greyed out on the comb filter types

Selecting "comb +" or "comb -" on the Wavetable or Oscillator node left
the cutoff knob unmovable. The UI derived "this filter has no cutoff"
from FilterStages() == 0, but a comb is a delay line, not a cascade of
SVF stages, so it legitimately reports zero stages while still reading
the cutoff knob as its tooth spacing ([file]:828). The DSP
was consuming the knob the whole time; only the UI thought otherwise.

Asking the stage count a question it was never meant to answer is the
kind of mistake the next filter family repeats, so the fix is a named
predicate rather than a special case at the call site:
SynthModes::FilterUsesCutoff() answers exactly the question the UI is
asking. It still reports false for anything unrecognised, which keeps
an out-of-range saved filterType degrading to a bypass the same way
FilterStages() gives the render path.

The four other filter-knob sites (Metallic, WaveTerrain, Equation,
ImageSpectral, Analog) gate on their own node-local index 0 and were
never affected, because comb was appended last to the enum.
query_subject: Fix the cutoff knob being greyed out on the comb filter types

subject: Fix note-wiring stuck-note race, cursor wrap-around, and audio-thread allocations
query_full:
Fix note-wiring stuck-note race, cursor wrap-around, and audio-thread allocations

RebuildAudioTopology() used to mutate live AudioNode/NoteEventQueue cursors
directly on the main thread while the audio thread could still be running the
previous ProcessList over the same objects - a race that could skip or
duplicate note events, including lost note-offs (stuck notes). It now only
describes the wiring (AudioTopology::noteOutboxes/noteWires);
AudioEngine::ApplyNoteWiringIfNew applies it once per generation on whichever
thread actually owns that ProcessList, carrying cursor positions forward from
what each consumer last applied.

Also: NoteEventQueue's overflow-protection cursor pick now weighs backlog
instead of raw ring index (fixed a wrap-around bug), the overflow tail
publish is memory_order_release to match the normal path, several
audio-thread scratch buffers move from static thread_local (lazily allocated
per CoreAudio IO thread on macOS) to plain AudioEngine members, and
ParamMailbox asserts on an out-of-range paramId in debug builds instead of
silently dropping it.

Adds NOTEREWIRESTRESSTEST: a Note Sequencer fanned to two synths with the
topology forced to rebuild every block for ~2s of notes, asserting zero
stuck voices and zero ring overflow.
query_subject: Fix note-wiring stuck-note race, cursor wrap-around, and audio-thread allocations

subject: Fix Drum Sequencer use-after-free and persist macOS MIDI device ids
query_full:
Fix Drum Sequencer use-after-free and persist macOS MIDI device ids

Drum Sequencer: voices cached a raw pointer to their lane's sample buffer;
swapping a lane's buffer retired the old one, the main thread freed it,
and still-sounding voices read freed memory (SIGSEGV on the audio thread).
Voices not reading the lane's new buffer are now dropped at swap time.

subject: Fix HDRI background seam with seam-safe textureGrad sampling
query_full:
Fix HDRI background seam with seam-safe textureGrad sampling

texture() at the equirect u=0/1 wrap relied on implicit screen-space
derivatives, which blow up right at the wrap (u jumps ~1 to ~0 between
adjacent fragments) and force the smallest mip - a thin vertical line
of the image's average colour up the sky. Sample twice, once as-is and
once shifted half a turn so its own wrap lands away from this
fragment, and feed textureGrad() whichever pair of derivatives is
small. The reflection path (sampleEnv, textureLod) was already correct
and is untouched; dirToEquirect has only these two call sites in the
codebase.

query_full:
fix(video/macos): VideoFrameAt returns true only for a new frame

[file] says a false return means "nothing new, skip the upload", and
Windows already behaves that way. macOS handed back the cached frame on every
request, so a 30 fps clip on a 60 Hz loop re-uploaded each frame twice (B8
finding 2: 268 uploads for 68-99 new frames).

The handle now remembers the pts it last delivered. A request that lands on
that frame again returns false and leaves the caller's pixels alone. A
caller with an empty buffer (a freshly adopted handle) always gets the frame.

VIDEOSPEEDTEST counted repeats as updates. It now expects the source frames
each phase actually crossed.

B8 after: uploads == new frames at every variant (2x1080 70/70, 4x1080 92/92,
2x2160 134/134, 4x2160 268/268).

subject: fix(video/macos): no per-frame 33 MB copy or cache entry during playback
query_full:
fix(video/macos): no per-frame 33 MB copy or cache entry during playback

B8 finding 3. Every decoded frame was zero-filled, copied into the caller,
and copied again into a fresh LRU cache entry: PushCacheFrame 47%,
`outPixels = pending` 14% and bzero 5% of the 4x2160 profile.

- Decoded frames rotate through two per-handle buffers (pending, current).
  The chosen frame is swapped to the caller. No allocation, no copy.
- DecodeNext resizes instead of assign(), so there is no per-frame clear.
- Only a backward reader rebuild fills the cache: its lookback span is what
  reverse playback asks for next. Forward playback never revisits a frame.
- Evicted cache buffers go to a small pool that the next push reuses.
- A request still inside the delivered frame (paused, or 60 Hz over 30 fps)
  returns before touching the reader. A finished reader holds its last frame
  instead of being rebuilt every cook.
- TryUseCache now matches only the frame that covers the request. Its
  1.25-frame + 10 ms window served frame N-1 for frame N. With every frame
  cached, that made an offline export at 30 fps repeat every other frame on
  main (new VIDEOEXACTTEST: 30 of 60 frames wrong at 30 fps, 60 of 120 at
  60 fps, 12 of 48 at 24 fps, plus a wrong seek to the last frame).

New VIDEOEXACTTEST (video group + full suite): records a clip whose frame i
is a grey unique to i, then steps VideoFrameAt through it in offline mode at
30/60/24 fps plus scattered seeks. It checks each request shows exactly the
covering source frame. Now 0 wrong.

B8 (1 run, frame p50 / decoded fps / dropped):
2x1080 8.4 ms / 30.0 / 0, 4x1080 9.5 / 30.1 / 0,
2x2160 8.7 / 29.7 / 0, 4x2160 9.9 / 29.8 / 2

subject: fix(video): bounded catch-up per cook on macOS, exact frames for offline renders
query_full:
fix(video): bounded catch-up per cook on macOS, exact frames for offline renders

B8 finding 8, the catch-up spiral: a clip that fell behind decoded, converted
and copied every frame in between inside one cook. That made the cook slower,
which put the clip further behind (4x2160 baseline: 1 run in 3 at 300 ms
frames, ~1640 drops, 23.5 fps).

macOS ([file]):
- Frames stay in decoder memory (retained CMSampleBuffer) until one is
  chosen. Only that one is converted, straight into the caller's buffer.
  Frames skipped while catching up cost their decode and nothing else. The
  pending/current pixel buffers are gone.
- Each VideoFrameAt call stops at a 6 ms decode budget (about two 4K frames
  on an M2). A clip that fell behind shows the newest frame it reached and
  continues next cook. VideoDecodeIsCatchingUp now reports this (it was
  constant false). A backward rebuild is exempt: its frames feed the reverse
  cache.
- Not done: restarting the reader at the target when more than ~2 frames
  behind. B8 measured a reader restart at 2160 at ~95 ms p50 (reader setup
  plus decode from the keyframe), against ~2-4 ms per decoded-and-skipped
  frame. A restart only pays off past about 1 s, which is the existing
  forward-resume window.

Realtime vs offline gate (shared):
- [file] gains inline VideoFrameAtExact. It keeps calling VideoFrameAt
  while VideoDecodeIsCatchingUp (bounded to 2 s), then once more.
- VideoSourceNode uses it when Transport is in offline mode. Realtime never
  waits.
- The gate lives in the caller because [file] is also linked into
  infinite-vst3-scanner, which has no Transport.
- On Windows and Linux, offline export now also waits for the decode thread
  (their VideoDecodeIsCatchingUp is unchanged). Before, it took whatever frame
  was ready. VideoFrameAt's contract is unchanged on all three.

VIDEOEXACTTEST now steps through VideoFrameAtExact, the node's offline path:
0 wrong frames at 30/60/24 fps and 0 wrong seeks. Pixel hashes are still
identical to the old conversion on b8_1080p30_0 and b8_2160p30_0 (60/60).

B8 (1 run, frame p50 / p99 / decoded fps / dropped):
2x1080 8.5 / 20.5 / 30.2 / 2, 4x1080 9.9 / 17.8 / 29.9 / 0,
2x2160 8.5 / 20.7 / 30.2 / 0, 4x2160 10.4 / 43.0 / 30.1 / 0
This did not move the ladder beyond noise: after the previous commit the
spiral no longer reproduces at 4 clips (the fixture maximum). The budget is
a guard on the worst case, not a steady-state win.

CI must verify: [file] (all 3), [file] (all 3).

subject: fix(video/macos): one frame of readahead, no starvation, rewind in place at the loop
query_full:
fix(video/macos): one frame of readahead, no starvation, rewind in place at the loop

The 3-run B8 AFTER set at 4x2160 paged on 8 GB (1.9 GB footprint, ~1 s
loop stalls, ~270 drops per clip) and the decode thread starved when it
could not keep up in real time.

- Readahead 1 and one spare recycled buffer instead of 2 + 3: a 4K RGBA
  frame is 33 MB per slot per clip.
- A frame still goes out every source-frame interval while decoding is
  behind, and the thread does not idle while behind, so a clip that
  cannot decode in real time plays slowly instead of freezing.
- The loop-point standby is parked only once the stream has run out,
  by rewinding that same reader (supportsRandomAccess +
  resetForReadingTimeRanges): no second decoder session, and 20-60 ms
  instead of 40-180 ms at 4x2160, so it is ready before the wrap.
- The parked point is the earliest wrap target seen for that loop point,
  and a wrap is matched against the parked frame's pts, so a wrap that
  lands a hair earlier or a cook later still uses it.

query_full:
fix(projector): pace projector windows to their own display's refresh

With a projector open the loop waits on the primary Output display's
refresh clock (Platform::WaitForDisplayRefresh: CVDisplayLink on macOS,
DXGI WaitForVBlank on Windows, a steady timer on Linux) right before the
projectors present, and every context swaps at interval 0. It no longer
depends on the canvas's swap blocking, which macOS skips for an occluded
or hidden window. Rate is a whole divisor of R (>= 60 fps), native R only
with headroom. Offline export/record takes stay unpaced; every main-context
glfwSwapInterval now goes through SetCanvasSwapInterval so ending a take
with a projector open can't stack two vsync waits.

the projectors on top of the canvas.
